checks: Compared frozen bytes field-by-field. The statement and metadata are identical; the only proof diff replaces the prose “at least twice” by 2 times a bracketed complete lower bound. The direction argument and all other proof text already agree in both frozen versions.

Rechecked the changed step: summing the two cap outer-row expressions gives two copies of the full top mass and bottom tails at b−c and b+c. The transport bound is applied twice, cancels the two top tails, and incurs two copies of the same possible loss. The revised bracket exactly matches that bound and the subsequent per-half computation.

Verified source 96f963f75f5ed816, §§1–4 and (1)–(9), against its digest. The archived result states at least 2s+1 maximizing bases and explicitly leaves exhaustiveness open. The final census paragraph is a documented normalization extension, checked directly below.

The inequalities for C_s are affine after splitting each absolute value, and 0 is a strict interior point. For q=−1,0,1 the radii are 7s+4, 4s+2, s and interval half-widths 1, 2, 3. The counts sum to 24s+15 and their length-weighted total is 72s+44.

On the three rows H_+ and H_− each take lengths 0, 2, 4, and at least one contains every middle or top mark. The other two caps take lengths 1, 0, 0: middle and top are excluded by 2−3<0 and 3−6<0. They cover the bottom, each at mass 14s+9<T_s. All four product caps ignore w.

For a≥0 reflection in p sends the margin for −a to the margin for +a increased by 2as. In F(a,b,c), the bottom tail threshold is b−c and reflecting x in the top source makes its complement the top tail at b+c. The projected distributions are atomless, so weak and strict tail endpoints have the same mass.

The three receiving blocks are even 0,…,4s, odd 1,…,4s+1, and 4s+2,…,6s+2; they are disjoint labeled fibers inside the actual shifted bottom index range. Each map preserves length and projects by the listed increment. At any threshold only the last block can lose mass, at most (2−Na)_+ per piece. Using both thresholds in the c,−c pair cancels both top tails.

The symmetric middle block has 6s+5 fibers and contributes 4 each to the pair after matching (k,c) with (−k,−c). The other 2s indices sum to s(8s+5) in absolute value. For v≤2, clipping the two v±c terms gives at least 2(v)_+ in each remaining pair. The combined lower bounds simplify to T_s+(3s+2)a for a≤2/N and T_s+2 for a≥2/N, per half of the pair.

Parallel translation through the anchor only removes mass. With nonzero x coefficient, reflection and rescaling give the paired expression. For the product, integrate c=v·w using central symmetry. If the x coefficient is zero, perturb by ηx, preserving the through-mark condition. The upper limit of the indicators is dominated by the original closed-cap indicator, so finite-measure reverse Fatou retains the lower bound even with entire boundary fibers. Reflection in p and the halfspace endpoint property then give the lower bound at every stated mark.

The bottom cap excludes all its bases from the maximizing census. Every top mark and every middle mark with x≠0 is strictly in an H_± cap. Raising its threshold by a small ε in (0,2) retains the mark and loses exactly ε of each middle fiber, hence positive mass. This argument is independent of w.

For j=s+1,…,r, t=4 suffices for x+t(p−j)≥0: |x|≤3 and every nonzero integer gap has magnitude at least one. The top is excluded, and bottom and middle keep every p>j fiber and half of the p=j fiber. The mass is 2(R−j)+1+4(r−j)+2, with its largest value 24s+13 at j=s+1. Reflection handles negative j, and the same cap excludes every lifted x=0 mark at those bases. All cases are exhausted without claiming a full product mark census.

Independently expanded 3T_s=M_s−2 and 8T_s−M_s=120s+68>0. An exact arithmetic check verified counts, cap costs, label disjointness and coefficients for s=1,…,40 and checked the paired cap inequality on a rational parameter grid for s=1,…,5. The symbolic proof handles all real parameters and integer s.

overlap.comparison: Its bound on maximizing points and bases assumes d≥2 with Hausdorff-null supporting sections. The product example has supporting facets {±h_q}×L of positive section measure, so that bound does not cover this family. The one-dimensional example is also outside its dimension hypothesis.

Its parity bound assumes an ambient differentiability property of an attaining cap at every maximum. The frozen construction establishes unbounded maximizing bases for ordinary depth without that premise. These are compatible statements with distinct scope.

initial_review.readability: The distributions B_a and U_a are pushforwards of disjoint labeled fiber sources. Their intervals can overlap after projection to the scalar line, which is harmless because the transport counts each labeled source only once. The extra census beyond the source is established in the final proof paragraph.
